```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
res <- readRDS(params$result)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7.8, fig.height = 3.9, dpi = 120)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  legend.position = "bottom"))
stage_labels <- c(exact = "Exact PLD", finite = "Finite samples", pulse = "M rises",
  constant_m = "M constant")
arm_labels <- c(full = "Full PLD", positive = "Positive density only", lognormal = "Lognormal")
fit_rows <- bind_rows(lapply(res$stages, function(stage) {
  bind_rows(lapply(stage, function(history) {
    bind_rows(lapply(history$fits, function(fit) {
      data.frame(stage = fit$stage, id = fit$id, arm = fit$arm, passed = fit$converged,
        gradient = if (is.null(fit$gradient)) NA_real_ else fit$gradient,
        error = fit$error, warnings = length(fit$warnings))
    }))
  }))
}))
study_fits <- function(result) unlist(lapply(result$stages, function(stage) {
  unlist(lapply(stage, "[[", "fits"), recursive = FALSE)
}), recursive = FALSE)
saved_fits <- study_fits(res)
default <- if (nzchar(params$default_result)) readRDS(params$default_result)
tight <- if (nzchar(params$tight_result)) readRDS(params$tight_result)
spatial <- if (nzchar(params$spatial_result)) readRDS(params$spatial_result)
simulated <- Filter(function(x) !is.null(x$audit), spatial$histories)
fits <- bind_rows(lapply(simulated, function(history) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(history$fits), function(age) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(history$fits[[age]]), function(arm) {
      x <- history$fits[[age]][[arm]]
      notes <- if (is.null(x$value$numerical)) "" else {
        paste(subset(x$value$numerical, status != "pass")$check, collapse = ", ")
      }
      data.frame(id = history$id, age = as.integer(age), arm = arm,
        passed = isTRUE(x$value$converged), elapsed = x$elapsed,
        why = if (!x$ok) x$error else notes)
    }))
  }))
}))
summarize_pairs <- function(table_name) {
  bind_rows(lapply(simulated, function(history) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(history$fits), function(age) {
      models <- history$fits[[age]]
      if (!all(vapply(models, function(x) isTRUE(x$value$converged), logical(1L)))) return(NULL)
      bind_rows(lapply(names(models), function(arm) {
        data <- models[[arm]]$value[[table_name]]
        mutate(as.data.frame(data), id = history$id, plus = as.integer(age), arm = arm)
      }))
    }))
  }))
}
spatial_metrics <- summarize_pairs("metrics")
spatial_pairs <- if (nrow(spatial_metrics)) {
  merge(filter(spatial_metrics, arm == "PLD"), filter(spatial_metrics, arm == "Lognormal"),
    by = c("id", "plus", "quantity"), suffixes = c("_pld", "_ln")) |>
    mutate(change = absolute_pld - absolute_ln)
}
passed_fits <- Filter(function(fit) fit$converged, saved_fits)
value_rows <- function(table) {
  bind_rows(lapply(passed_fits, function(fit) {
    value <- fit$values[[table]]
    if (!is.null(value)) mutate(value, stage = fit$stage, id = fit$id, arm = fit$arm)
  }))
}
metrics <- value_rows("metrics")
mortality <- value_rows("mortality")
interval <- function(x) {
  n <- length(x)
  half <- if (n >= 2) qt(0.975, n - 1L) * sd(x) / sqrt(n) else NA_real_
  c(mean = mean(x), lower = mean(x) - half, upper = mean(x) + half)
}
compare <- function(rows, outcomes, keys) {
  left <- rows[rows$arm == "full", c(keys, outcomes)]
  right <- rows[rows$arm != "full", c(keys, outcomes, "arm")]
  both <- merge(left, right, by = keys, suffixes = c("_full", "_reference"))
  bind_rows(lapply(outcomes, function(outcome) {
    value <- both[[paste0(outcome, "_full")]] - both[[paste0(outcome, "_reference")]]
    both |>
      mutate(difference = value) |>
      filter(is.finite(difference)) |>
      group_by(across(all_of(c(setdiff(keys, "id"), "arm")))) |>
      summarise(n = n(), change = interval(difference)[["mean"]],
        lower = interval(difference)[["lower"]], upper = interval(difference)[["upper"]],
        .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(outcome = outcome)
  }))
}
paired <- if (nrow(metrics)) compare(metrics, "absolute", c("stage", "id", "metric"))
old_pairs <- if (nrow(paired)) filter(paired, metric == "Age 14+ abundance")
m_pairs <- if (nrow(mortality)) compare(mortality, "absolute", c("stage", "id"))
describe <- function(rows, lead) {
  if (!NROW(rows)) return(paste0(lead, " had no numerical pairs."))
  sprintf("%s changed error by %+.4f (95%% interval %.4f to %.4f, %d pairs).",
    lead, rows$change, rows$lower, rows$upper, rows$n)
}
```

## Abstract

We simulated 30 years of catches and surveys to test whether the Poisson-link
delta lognormal (PLD) improves estimates when sampling produces zeros. For
age 14+ abundance, error is the mean absolute log ratio of estimates to truth.
`r describe(if (NROW(old_pairs)) filter(old_pairs, stage == "exact", arm == "positive"), "Adding encounter information to the same positive-value likelihood")`
`r describe(if (NROW(old_pairs)) filter(old_pairs, stage == "exact", arm == "lognormal"), "Using full PLD instead of an ordinary lognormal under exact PLD sampling")`
`r describe(if (NROW(old_pairs)) filter(old_pairs, stage == "finite"), "Using fitted PLD instead of an ordinary lognormal with finite age samples")`
`r describe(if (NROW(m_pairs)) filter(m_pairs, stage == "pulse"), "Adding encounter information for the estimated rise in natural mortality, measured as mean absolute error per year")`

```{r spatial-abstract, results='asis'}
if (is.null(spatial)) {
  cat("The whole-area SimSurvey experiment has no completed checkpoints.")
} else {
  cat(spatial$gate)
  old <- if (NROW(spatial_pairs)) filter(spatial_pairs, plus == 20L, quantity == "Age 14+ abundance")
  if (NROW(old)) {
    difference <- interval(old$change)
    cat(sprintf(" On %d paired whole-area SimSurvey histories, fitted PLD changed age-14+ error by %+.3f (95%% interval %.3f to %.3f).",
      nrow(old), difference[1L], difference[2L], difference[3L]))
  }
}
```

## Simulated population and observations

Each independent 30-year history follows ages 1–14+. Years 5–7 and 16–18 have
recruitment at 40% of the usual level. The oldest age includes survivors from
ages 13 and 14+. Fully selected fishing mortality changes from 0.06 to 0.22 to
0.035 per year in years 1–7, 8–12 and 13–30. Natural mortality is 0.25 through
year 13 and 0.60 thereafter. The constant-M control keeps it at 0.25.
The survey index equals abundance at age before fishing.

PLD assigns a zero probability of \(2^{-\mu/y_{50}}\), where \(\mu\) is the
mean across all observations and \(y_{50}\) is the value where half the samples
are zero. After a positive encounter, a lognormal with arithmetic mean
\(\mu/(1-P(Y=0))\) gives the observed amount. The positive-density comparison
uses this same density and omits the encounter indicator likelihood.
The ordinary lognormal uses \(\mu\) as its median and excludes zeros.
[Poisson-link delta model](https://doi.org/10.1139/cjfas-2017-0266)

In the finite-sample experiment, fish in each annual age sample follow a
multinomial distribution. We multiply their proportions by a noisy annual
total centered on the true total. This retains dependence among age
observations. We estimate the PLD detection scale and one log-SD per stream.
In the exact PLD comparison the observation log-SDs and detection scales
are supplied. Calibration used six independent histories and matched the
expected share of zeros across ages 2–14+, excluding age 1.

```{r calibration}
knitr::kable(res$calibration$values, digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Program", "Target zero fraction", "PLD half-detection (thousand fish)",
    "Exact PLD zeros", "Fish aged per year", "Finite-sample zeros"))
```

```{r zeros, fig.cap="Sampled zero fractions by age in each observation experiment. The last age pools all fish aged 14 and older."}
zeros <- bind_rows(lapply(names(res$stages)[1:2], function(stage) {
  bind_rows(lapply(res$stages[[stage]], function(history) mutate(history$zeros, stage = stage)))
}))
if (nrow(zeros)) {
  zeros |>
    group_by(stage, component, age) |>
    summarise(zero = sum(zeros) / sum(observed), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(experiment = unname(stage_labels[stage]),
      program = recode(component, catch = "Catch", index = "Survey")) |>
    ggplot(aes(age, zero, colour = experiment)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    facet_wrap(~program) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 4, 7, 10, 14), labels = c(1, 4, 7, 10, "14+")) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Exact PLD" = "#126782", "Finite samples" = "#C44C27")) +
    labs(x = "Age", y = "Sampled zeros", colour = NULL)
}
```

## Fit reliability

The fits estimate three fishing mortality levels, a shared normal-shaped
selectivity curve, and two recruitment levels. Catchability is fixed at one.
The mortality comparisons estimate early and late M with the change at year
14 specified in advance. Each comparison used the same starting values for
shared parameters and a maximum gradient threshold of 0.01. A stage
expanded after at least seven of eight histories passed in every comparison
within that stage. Both mortality scenarios had to pass before either expanded.

```{r optimizer, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(default)) {
  attempts <- study_fits(default)
  failures <- Filter(function(fit) !fit$converged, attempts)
  failed_checks <- unique(unlist(lapply(failures, function(fit) {
    with(fit$numerical, check[status != "pass"])
  })))
  gradients <- range(vapply(failures, function(fit) fit$gradient, numeric(1)))
  cat(sprintf(paste("The original run used the package optimizer settings.",
    "%d attempts failed numerical checks, all on %s (%.4f–%.4f).",
    "The exact PLD experiment passed the expansion gate. The finite-sample and mortality",
    "experiments stopped at eight histories.\n\n"),
    length(failures), paste(failed_checks, collapse = ", "), gradients[1L], gradients[2L]))
  original_gate <- transform(default$gate, stage = unname(stage_labels[stage]),
    reference = unname(arm_labels[reference]))
  print(knitr::kable(original_gate,
    col.names = c("Original experiment", "Compared with full PLD", "Original pairs out of eight")))
}
if (!is.null(tight)) {
  cat(paste("A second pilot tightened the relative optimizer tolerance to 1e-13.",
    "Singular convergence codes reduced the number of usable pairs to zero across all",
    "five contrasts. Both pilot runs remain available with their original checks.\n\n"))
}
if (identical(res$provenance$optimizer, "newton")) {
  refined <- sum(vapply(saved_fits, function(fit) isTRUE(fit$study_newton), logical(1L)))
  cat(sprintf(paste("For the final run, the usual optimizer was followed by one common",
    "damped Newton step using the RTMB Hessian. The step was accepted when it reduced both",
    "the objective and the maximum absolute gradient. It was accepted for %d of %d attempts.",
    "The numerical acceptance checks remained the same.\n"), refined, length(saved_fits)))
} else if (identical(res$provenance$optimizer, "tight")) {
  cat("All arms used a relative optimizer tolerance of 1e-13.\n")
}
```

```{r reliability}
gates <- transform(res$gate, stage = unname(stage_labels[stage]),
  reference = unname(arm_labels[reference]))
knitr::kable(gates, col.names = c("Experiment", "Compared with full PLD", "Pilot pairs out of eight"))
fit_summary <- fit_rows |>
  group_by(stage, arm) |>
  summarise(attempted = n(), passed = sum(passed), error = sum(nzchar(error)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(stage = unname(stage_labels[stage]), arm = unname(arm_labels[arm]))
knitr::kable(fit_summary, col.names = c("Experiment", "Model", "Attempts", "Passes", "Errors"))
```

## Did the fits recover abundance?

For each history we average absolute log error over years 16–23 for the
14+ age group. A negative change means that full PLD reduced error relative
to the model it is compared with. We also compare ages 2–8 of the weak
cohorts, recruitment during weak years, and annual spawning stock biomass
(SSB). Intervals summarize paired differences across independent histories.

```{r population, fig.cap="Change in mean absolute log error with full PLD. Points show the mean across numerically successful pairs, with 95% intervals. Negative values favor full PLD."}
if (NROW(paired)) {
  paired |>
    filter(stage %in% c("exact", "finite")) |>
    mutate(experiment = unname(stage_labels[stage]), Compared = unname(arm_labels[arm])) |>
    ggplot(aes(change, metric, colour = Compared)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), orientation = "y",
      width = 0.16, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
    geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~experiment) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Positive density only" = "#126782", "Lognormal" = "#C44C27")) +
    labs(x = "Full PLD minus comparison model", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
}
```

```{r bias}
if (nrow(metrics)) {
  bias_table <- filter(metrics, stage %in% c("exact", "finite")) |>
    group_by(stage, arm, metric) |>
    summarise(n = n(), bias = mean(bias), coverage = mean(coverage),
      interval_width = mean(width), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(stage = unname(stage_labels[stage]), arm = unname(arm_labels[arm]))
  knitr::kable(bias_table, digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Experiment", "Model", "Quantity", "Passed", "Signed log error",
      "Coverage", "Mean log interval width"))
}
```

Coverage and interval width refer to fits that passed for each individual
model. Age-specific abundance intervals are unavailable. Interpretation of
paired error changes uses the same histories in both models.

## Did the encounter indicator help estimate a rise in M?

The change is late M minus early M. A false increase occurs in the
constant-M control when the lower 95% limit exceeds zero. The intervals
use a Wald approximation for the contrast on the per-year scale.

```{r mortality}
if (nrow(mortality)) {
  change <- compare(mortality, "absolute", c("stage", "id"))
  knitr::kable(mutate(change, stage = unname(stage_labels[stage]),
    arm = unname(arm_labels[arm]))[c("stage", "arm", "n", "change", "lower", "upper")],
    digits = 3, col.names = c("Scenario", "Compared with full PLD", "Pairs",
      "Change in absolute error", "Lower", "Upper"))
  tab <- mortality |>
    group_by(stage, arm) |>
    summarise(n = n(), bias = mean(bias), coverage = mean(coverage),
      width = mean(upper - lower), positive = sum(positive), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(stage = unname(stage_labels[stage]), arm = unname(arm_labels[arm]))
  knitr::kable(tab, digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Scenario", "Model", "Passed", "Bias", "Coverage", "Mean interval width",
      "Intervals above zero"))
}
```

```{r mortality-fig, fig.cap="Changes in natural mortality estimated from each history. Vertical bars are Wald intervals. The dashed line gives the true change in each scenario."}
if (nrow(mortality)) {
  mortality <- mutate(mortality, scenario = unname(stage_labels[stage]),
    model = unname(arm_labels[arm]))
  ggplot(mortality, aes(id, estimate, colour = model)) +
    geom_hline(data = distinct(mortality, scenario, truth),
      aes(yintercept = truth), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.15,
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.45)) +
    geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.45), size = 1.5) +
    facet_wrap(~scenario) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Full PLD" = "#258375", "Positive density only" = "#126782")) +
    labs(x = "History", y = "Late minus early M (per year)", colour = NULL)
}
```

Under exact PLD sampling, the improvement over the ordinary lognormal occurred
mostly through the different model for positive amounts. The paired comparison
with that density held fixed isolated little contribution from encountering a
zero or a positive value. With finite age samples the older-age improvement is
uncertain. Precise mortality estimates in both fits reflect the constrained test
design.

Known survey catchability anchors population scale. The mortality test supplies
the year of the change and uses simple age-shared M. The finite-sample
comparisons evaluate a departure from exact PLD under the same stock history
and fixed sampling effort. Both studies retained failed attempts, numerical
checks and source hashes in their checkpoints.



## Whole-area SimSurvey experiment

We simulated the same stock over 30 years using SimSurvey's default recruitment,
growth, weight, maturity and space–age–year distribution. One fishery with a
dome-shaped selectivity curve and one RV survey with an ascending logistic curve
operate throughout a 40 × 40 grid. Fisheries monitor half of operations and sample
up to 150 fish per sampled operation. The survey uses two sets per 1,000 square
kilometres, measures up to 100 fish and ages up to three per length group and
set. The simulated total mortality at age is

\[
Z_{ta}=0.30+F^{\mathrm{full}}_t \exp\{-\tfrac12[(a-7.7)/2.5]^2\}.
\]

Fully selected fishing mortality starts at 0.12 per year, follows a log-scale
random walk with an innovation SD of 0.10, and triples relative to its
underlying path during years 14–16. Recruitment varies independently of
spawning biomass. The maximum age is a 20+ group, with survivors retained
from the second year onward. Fish in that group use age-20 biology and
selectivity. The first-year age profile follows exponential survival as in
tinyAM's initialization.
[SimSurvey study](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0232822)

### Did the simulated fishery approximate constant M?

SimSurvey aims for the catch implied by the specified fishing rate. Its
realized removals can vary around the implied age composition. Mortality
accounting uses \(M^{\mathrm{realized}}_{ta}=Z_{ta}-F^{\mathrm{realized}}_{ta}\).
The study proceeds after the first two histories pass checks on the input
population, survey and catch data. For ages 5–10 we require a
population-weighted mean absolute departure from 0.30 of at most 0.03 per
year, and no annual population-weighted mean more than 0.06 from 0.30.
Expansion from eight to 24 histories also requires at least seven successful
age-20+ pairs.

```{r spatial-accounting}
if (length(simulated)) {
  audit <- bind_rows(lapply(simulated, "[[", "audit"))
  knitr::kable(audit, digits = 3,
    col.names = c("History", "Mean absolute M departure", "Largest annual mean M departure",
      "Catch target shortfalls", "Within tolerance"))
}
```

```{r spatial-mortality, fig.cap="Fishing and natural mortality across ages 5–10. Lines average across age using true population weights, separately for each history. The shaded band marks the fishing pulse."}
if (length(simulated)) {
  rates <- bind_rows(lapply(simulated, function(h) mutate(h$reference, id = h$id))) |>
    filter(age %in% 5:10, N > 0) |>
    group_by(id, year) |>
    summarise(
      F_reference = stats::weighted.mean(F_reference, N),
      F_realized = stats::weighted.mean(F_realized, N),
      M_reference = spatial$M,
      M_realized = stats::weighted.mean(M_realized, N),
      .groups = "drop") |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(id, year), names_to = c("rate", "scenario"), names_sep = "_") |>
    mutate(rate = recode(rate, F = "Fishing mortality", M = "Natural mortality"),
      scenario = recode(scenario, reference = "Prescribed", realized = "Realized"))
  ggplot(rates, aes(year, value, group = interaction(id, scenario), colour = scenario)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = min(spatial$pulse) - 0.5, xmax = max(spatial$pulse) + 0.5,
      ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.13) +
    geom_line(alpha = if (length(simulated) > 2L) 0.35 else 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~rate, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Prescribed = "#126782", Realized = "#C44C27")) +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Mortality rate (per year)", colour = NULL)
}
```

### Where did sampling produce zeros?

A recorded zero counts as a sample outcome. Incomplete age assignment and
unsampled observations remain missing. Age 20+ has very low fishery
selectivity under the simulated dome. Survey detections may supply most of the
direct information there.

```{r spatial-zeros, fig.cap="Share of available observations reported as zero by age and year. Crosses mark age–years with missing observations. Age 20 includes all older fish."}
if (length(simulated)) {
  raw <- bind_rows(lapply(simulated, "[[", "observed"))
  observed <- raw |>
    group_by(component, year, age) |>
    summarise(available = sum(!is.na(obs)), missing = sum(is.na(obs)), zeros = sum(obs == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(zero = ifelse(available > 0, zeros / available, NA_real_),
      program = recode(component, catch = "Catch", index = "RV index"))
  ggplot(observed, aes(year, age, fill = zero)) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_point(data = filter(observed, missing > 0), shape = 4, size = 0.85) +
    facet_wrap(~program) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 14, 20), labels = c(1, 5, 10, 14, "20+")) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f4f9f9", high = "#126782", limits = c(0, 1),
      labels = scales::label_percent(), na.value = "grey85") +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Age", fill = "Sampled zeros")
}
```

```{r spatial-zero-counts}
if (length(simulated)) {
  bind_rows(mutate(raw, ages = "All ages"), mutate(filter(raw, age == 20L), ages = "20+ only")) |>
    group_by(component, ages) |>
    summarise(sampled = sum(!is.na(obs)), zeros = sum(obs == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      missing = sum(is.na(obs)), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(component = recode(component, catch = "Catch", index = "RV index"),
      fraction = zeros / sampled) |>
    knitr::kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Program", "Ages", "Sampled", "Zeros", "Missing",
      "Zero fraction among sampled"))
}
```

### Did PLD improve recovery?

The fits estimate annual fishing levels with a shared dome and use a logistic
survey catchability. In both fits,
`M_settings = list(process = "off", mu_supplied = ~ I(0.30))` fixes natural
mortality at the prescribed simulation value. The fits also share deterministic
cohort survival and a recruitment random walk with the generating innovation
SD of 0.50. PLD estimates a separate half-detection amount and log-SD for
each stream. The ordinary lognormal uses positive observations and estimates
one log-SD per stream. This comparison changes both the use of zeros and the
treatment of positive observations.

Our primary measure is mean absolute log error in age-14+ abundance in years
16–23. For the age-20+ fit we add ages 14 through 20+ together before scoring.
The first eight histories also use a model with age 14+ as the terminal
group. Its shared F over the pooled age group approximates the generating
dome's declining selectivity beyond age 14. Pooling can also remove zeros.
A PLD fit that estimates the detection scale requires at least one eligible
sampled zero in each fitted stream. The figures use only paired
numerically successful fits. Those histories can differ from the ones with
failures, so small paired samples describe limited evidence. The reliability
table includes every attempt.

```{r spatial-reliability}
if (nrow(fits)) {
  fits |>
    group_by(age, arm) |>
    summarise(attempts = n(), passes = sum(passed),
      reasons = paste(sort(unique(why[nzchar(why)])), collapse = ", "),
      .groups = "drop") |>
    knitr::kable(col.names = c("Plus age", "Model", "Attempts", "Passes", "Errors or failed checks"))
} else if (!is.null(spatial)) {
  errors <- vapply(spatial$histories, function(h) if (is.null(h$error)) "" else h$error,
    character(1L))
  if (any(nzchar(errors))) print(knitr::kable(data.frame(history = which(nzchar(errors)),
    error = errors[nzchar(errors)])))
}
```

```{r spatial-recovery, fig.cap="Paired change in absolute log error under PLD. A negative value favors PLD. Bars give 95% Monte Carlo intervals across histories."}
if (NROW(spatial_pairs)) {
  spatial_pairs |>
    group_by(plus, quantity) |>
    summarise(pairs = n(), mean = interval(change)[1L], lower = interval(change)[2L],
      upper = interval(change)[3L], .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(plus = paste0("Age ", plus, "+ fit")) |>
    ggplot(aes(mean, quantity)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
    geom_segment(aes(x = lower, xend = upper, yend = quantity), na.rm = TRUE, colour = "#126782") +
    geom_point(colour = "#126782", size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~plus) +
    labs(x = "PLD minus lognormal error", y = NULL)
}
```

```{r spatial-metrics}
if (nrow(spatial_metrics)) {
  spatial_metrics |>
    group_by(plus, arm, quantity) |>
    summarise(paired = n(), error = mean(absolute), bias = mean(bias),
      coverage = mean(coverage), .groups = "drop") |>
    knitr::kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Plus age", "Model", "Quantity", "Pairs",
      "Absolute log error", "Signed log error", "Mean coverage"))
}
```

```{r spatial-F, fig.cap="Annual fitted and realized fishing mortality averaged over ages 5–10 in the first available successful age-20+ pair. All curves use the true abundance weights."}
fishing <- summarize_pairs("F")
if (nrow(fishing) && any(fishing$plus == 20L)) {
  available <- filter(fishing, plus == 20L)
  example <- available |>
    filter(id == min(id)) |>
    select(year, model = arm, F = F_est)
  truth <- available |>
    filter(id == min(id)) |>
    distinct(year, F = F_realized) |>
    mutate(model = "Realized")
  ggplot(bind_rows(example, truth), aes(year, F, colour = model)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = min(spatial$pulse) - 0.5, xmax = max(spatial$pulse) + 0.5,
      ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.13) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Lognormal = "#126782", PLD = "#C44C27", Realized = "#333333")) +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Fishing mortality (per year)", colour = NULL)
}
```

```{r spatial-stock, fig.cap="Spawning biomass and age-14+ abundance in the first available successful age-20+ pair. Shading marks the fishing pulse."}
numbers <- summarize_pairs("N")
biomass <- summarize_pairs("ssb")
if (nrow(numbers) && any(numbers$plus == 20L)) {
  selected <- min(numbers$id[numbers$plus == 20L])
  older <- filter(numbers, id == selected, plus == 20L, age >= 14L) |>
    group_by(year, arm) |>
    summarise(value = sum(est), .groups = "drop")
  target <- simulated[[match(selected, vapply(simulated, "[[", integer(1L), "id"))]]$reference
  older_truth <- filter(target, age >= 14L) |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(value = sum(N), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(arm = "Truth")
  biomass <- filter(biomass, id == selected, plus == 20L)
  ggplot(bind_rows(
    mutate(bind_rows(older, older_truth), quantity = "Age 14+ (thousand fish)"),
    transmute(biomass, year, arm, value = est, quantity = "Spawning biomass (tonnes)"),
    mutate(distinct(biomass, year, value = truth), arm = "Truth", quantity = "Spawning biomass (tonnes)")),
    aes(year, value, colour = arm)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = min(spatial$pulse) - 0.5, xmax = max(spatial$pulse) + 0.5,
      ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.13) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~quantity, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Lognormal = "#126782", PLD = "#C44C27", Truth = "#333333")) +
    labs(x = "Year", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
}
```

## Conclusion

Under exact PLD sampling, the full likelihood improved older-age estimates
relative to ordinary lognormal. Holding the positive-value likelihood fixed
showed little additional benefit from whether a sample recorded zero. The
controlled mortality experiment likewise found little change in recovery of
the mortality increase from adding the encounter term. Results with finite
age samples were uncertain.

In the SimSurvey pilot, PLD had lower average error in abundance at ages
14 and older among successful pairs. The uncertainty included both an
improvement and a worsening. Numerical failures reduced the paired sample,
and the realized catch-at-age composition caused departures from the
prescribed constant M. Both limit what the pilot can tell us about the
contribution of sampled zeros to recovery.

PLD is useful as a sensitivity analysis when a survey or fishery records
many sampled zeros. Check where the zeros enter the fitted data after pooling
and compare both families on common held-out observations. The experiments
give limited evidence that adding the encounter likelihood alone improves
stock estimates consistently.
